templates_considered: requests_have_timeout (SEC-013): fits; timeout max 30 seconds on api.request and related statements
external_calls_handle_errors (LOG-010): fits; containment of external statements in try_catch
tls_verification_on (SEC-011): not requested by the ask
middleware_surfaces_errors (LOG-011): not relevant, no middleware in the ask
rate_limiting: not relevant to outbound timeouts

rules.covers: every external call finishes within 30 seconds (template rule)
every external call sets its timeout explicitly; added because param_bound judges an omitted timeout at its 10-second default and would pass it
every external call sits inside a try block so a vendor failure reaches error handling (template rule, statement list extended beyond the template to the full outbound set in the catalogue)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: the catch branch actually handles the failure sensibly
retries and backoff for failing calls (retry_failed_webhooks loops without delay)
a timeout actually fires within 30 seconds during a real vendor outage
ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.* calls bounded by a timeout
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists; these statements take no timeout parameter

assumptions: a 30-second maximum is an acceptable upper bound for every vendor call; the customer did not name one
a throw in the catch branch is the desired behaviour for payment, refund, quote and SMS calls
a failing shipping rate for one carrier should not stop the sync for the others
the throw statement shape { name, value } is valid XanoScript; the dry run accepted it but did not exercise it at runtime
confusions: requests_have_timeout's limits text says an omitted timeout is judged at its 10-second default, so the template rule alone passes a call that sets no timeout; the template does not say to add param_required, and I added it from reading the catalogue
the skill says a throw/precondition is how callers see failures but gives no example of the throw statement's shape; I wrote throw { name, value } from the naming pattern and the parser accepted it

external_calls_handle_errors lists its limits as needing stream.from_request, ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.*.direct_query added to cover every outbound call, but the template's rule keeps only api.request; I extended the statements list myself

the template table lists SEC-013 and LOG-010 as separate templates, so the request covered two policies; the 'one policy per goal' guidance and the 'one policy per template' guidance point different ways for a request that spans two templates, and I followed the template rule

the brief's plan step asks for objects to build first, but for this ask the enforcement is changes to existing call sites; the plan format has no slot for 'wrap every existing call', so I used the changes section
wished_for: an example of throw in XanoScript, and of the common catch-then-rethrow pattern, in the policy-authoring skill or the kit
a note in SEC-013's limits or template fill saying to add a param_required rule when a timeout must be explicit, not just bounded
a template or recipe for the whole 'external calls are resilient' goal: timeouts plus try_catch plus catch behaviour, so the plan does not have to be assembled from two templates
guidance on retry loops (a while loop around an api.request with no delay) since they are a common way an external-call fix goes wrong
why_confidence: Every outbound api.request in the workspace now has an explicit timeout of 30 seconds or less and sits inside a try_catch, and both policies parsed and the dry run exited 0. Confidence is held at medium because I did not run xano policy evaluate, so which objects the rules judge is a prediction; the catch branches are only checked for existence, not for correct behaviour; and the ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.* calls cannot be bounded by a timeout at all, so the 'every external call has a timeout' part is only true for the five statements that take one.
